question: Explain Union-Find (disjoint set union). What do path compression and union by size do?

scenes.sub: Which group is this in? Merge two groups. Both in almost constant time.
scenes.say: Union Find, also called disjoint set union. It's the data structure for tracking groups that merge over time. Let's watch it work, then write it.

scenes.head: Think of a club fair
scenes.say: Picture a club fair. Every student wears a badge naming who they follow. Ben follows Ana. Cy follows Ben. Ana follows nobody, so she's the club president. Dev follows nobody either, so he's his own club. Are Cy and Ana in the same club? Follow the badges up to the end. Same president, same club. Merging two clubs just means one president starts following the other. That's Union Find.

scenes.head: Parents and groups
scenes.say: Use it whenever pairs get joined over time: friendships, network links, graph edges arriving one by one. Every element stores a parent. At the start each is its own parent, so six elements make six groups. Union zero and one: point one at zero. Groups drop to five. Union two and three: point three at two. Four groups. Now union one and three. Find the two roots and hang one root under the other. Three groups left.

scenes.head: Path compression
scenes.say: Without care, a chain can form. One points to zero, two points to one, three points to two. Finding the root of three takes three hops. That's the slow case. Path compression fixes it. While walking up, repoint every node straight at the root. After one find of three, two and three both point at zero. The next find takes a single hop. Same answers, much flatter tree.

scenes.head: The whole structure
scenes.say: Here it is in C plus plus. The constructor makes every element its own parent, using iota, and every size one. Find is recursive. If x is its own parent, it's the root. Otherwise find the root of its parent, and store the answer back into p of x. That single assignment is path compression. Unite finds both roots. Same root means already joined, so return false. Otherwise hang the smaller tree under the bigger one. That's union by size.

scenes.head: Counting components, spotting cycles
scenes.say: Count components. Five nodes, four edges. The first three edges each merge two groups, so the count drops each time. The fourth edge, two to zero, joins nodes already connected, so unite returns false. That's cycle detection. Two components left. With both tricks, each operation costs inverse Ackermann of n, under five for any real input. Call it constant. Classics: Number of Provinces, Redundant Connection, Accounts Merge, and Kruskal's algorithm. Follow-up: can it delete edges? Not directly. Go offline, or use rollback.

Because edges arrive online, and Union Find answers instantly. The common mistake: comparing parents instead of roots. Always call find first.

scenes.say: Each element points to a parent, and the root names the group. Find the root, and unite two roots. With path compression and union by size, each operation is nearly constant time.
